comparator.name: Artificial Intelligence
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 programme page and TER define a 180-EC bachelor: a 150-EC major and a genuine 30-EC minor. Years one and two each contain twelve compulsory 5-EC courses. Year three contains a 15-EC specialisation, a 15-EC bachelor project and the 30-EC minor. The TER lists five coherent specialisations. Computational Neuroscience is reconstructed by the neutral official-order tie-break; its Cognitive Neuroscience course is introduced in 2027-2028, the academic year in which a Fall 2026 entrant reaches year three.

Machine learning, data analysis, neural networks and computational optimisation

Ethics and philosophy of artificial intelligence and cognition
Scientific methods, communication and independent artificial-intelligence project work
questions: How intelligence can be understood, modelled and designed in humans and machines

routeSelection.basis: The official programme page and TER list five coherent specialisations—Computational Neuroscience, Hybrid Intelligence, Language and AI, Machine Learning, and Robotics—without establishing one as the broadest or default route. Computational Neuroscience is listed first and is therefore selected as a neutral official-order tie-break, without reference to UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the broad artificial-intelligence core spanning programming, algorithms, logic, machine learning, autonomous systems, robotics, cognition, ethics and decision-making. Machine Learning and Computational AI supports a distinct software, algorithms and data-intensive curriculum. Cognitive Neuroscience and Hybrid Intelligence supports a third curriculum centred on brain, behaviour, perception, language and human-machine questions. Language and AI and Robotics remain evidenced directions but are not attempted after the three-alternative maximum. Curricular-topic rows support these directions; illustrative and outcome rows remain search-only.

alternatives.label: Artificial Intelligence, Cognition and Autonomous Systems
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum integrates programming, logic, machine learning, computer vision, robotics and intelligent decision-making with brain, behaviour, perception, philosophy and ethics.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines computational AI, machine learning, autonomous systems and robotics with cognitive neuroscience, human behaviour, language, philosophy and responsible technology.
progression: Programming, data science, brain and behaviour, mathematics, databases and computer vision precede advanced machine learning, robotics, optimisation, perception, neural networks, reinforcement learning and psycholinguistics. The schedule follows planned terms; all prerequisites occur earlier and eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Machine Learning and Computational AI
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum foregrounds software, algorithms, databases, machine learning, neural networks, optimisation and reinforcement learning, supported by statistics, philosophy and empirical methods.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses differ from the closest match, replacing robotics, perception, computer vision and psycholinguistics with networks and operating systems, software development, advanced algorithms and an advanced research seminar. This meets the 30-EC/four-course floor and creates a more software- and algorithm-intensive direction.
alternatives.concept: A computational route emphasising software systems, algorithms, data management, machine learning, neural networks, optimisation and reinforcement learning, with quantitative research and responsible-AI context.
progression: Programming, logic, data science, databases, mathematics and machine learning precede software development, advanced algorithms, neural networks, optimisation, reinforcement learning and advanced empirical research. The schedule follows planned terms; all prerequisites occur earlier and eight 300-level courses are included.
traceOverrides: studies neural-network and deep-learning methods as advanced machine-learning techniques in the computational route
develops optimisation methods used to train and analyse artificial-intelligence models
provides complementary study of human higher cognition and its neural bases

alternatives.label: Cognitive Neuroscience and Hybrid Intelligence
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres brain, cognition, behaviour, perception, language, social interaction, development, emotion and philosophical questions about mind and agency, while retaining an AI and data-science foundation.
alternatives.distinctness: Thirteen courses differ from the closest match and fifteen differ from the machine-learning route. The curriculum shifts substantially from specialised computational engineering toward cognitive neuroscience, behavioural science, psycholinguistics and philosophy while preserving programming, data, logic, agents and neural networks.
alternatives.concept: A human-centred route linking AI foundations to neurobiology, cognition, perception, social and developmental psychology, language, emotion, philosophy of mind and empirical research.
progression: Programming, data, brain and behaviour, neurobiology, psychology, logic and machine learning precede perception, neural networks, higher cognition, psycholinguistics, advanced research, development, emotion and philosophy. The schedule follows planned terms; all prerequisites occur earlier and nine 300-level courses are included.

blocks: Introduction to Programming directly teaches imperative programming, with broader UCR scope and different credits.
Algorithms & Data Structures directly covers algorithmic design and data structures at a later UCR level.
Mathematical Methods supplies quantitative foundations, but is not a dedicated calculus-for-AI course.
Linear Algebra directly covers the linear-algebra portion, without the full multivariable-calculus component.
Probability & Statistics supplies advanced probability and statistical modelling at different scope.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics directly covers formal logic and discrete structures.
Software Development includes object-oriented software design and development at different scope.
UCR distributes AI foundations across multiple courses rather than offering a selected one-to-one Fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence course.
UCR has no selected standalone Introduction to Artificial Intelligence course.
UCR offers one selected logic-and-discrete-mathematics course but no second advanced-logic course in the scheduled pathway.
UCR has no selected dedicated signals-and-systems course.
Machine learning, data and autonomous systems
Introduction to Data Science develops data analysis, visualisation and communication, with different scope and credits.
Machine Learning directly provides the introductory machine-learning foundation.
Neural Networks & Deep Learning directly studies neural computation, but does not reproduce the neuroscience specialisation course.
Optimization Methods in AI supports computational model fitting, but is not a dedicated brain-modelling course.
Decision-making in AI directly studies intelligent agents and computational choice, with narrower scope.
Reinforcement Learning is an applied machine-learning method focused on sequential decisions.
Robotics directly develops autonomous-system integration, with a robotics-specific emphasis.
UCR approaches architectures of intelligence across AI and cognitive-science courses rather than through one selected equivalent.
Introduction to Brain & Behavior includes cognitive psychology within a broader brain-and-behaviour foundation.
Neurobiology directly supplies an introduction to neural systems, with UCR-specific biological scope.
Higher Order Functions examines advanced cognition and neural bases, but is not identical to Groningen's new Cognitive Neuroscience course.
Psycholinguistics examines language processing in humans; it is adjacent to, not a computational natural-language-processing course.
UCR offers psycholinguistics but no selected general-linguistics foundation course.
Mind, ethics and responsible artificial intelligence
AI Ethics directly examines ethical issues in artificial intelligence.
Philosophy of Mind directly addresses philosophical questions about mind and cognition, with less AI-specific scope.
Research, project work and open choice
Advanced Research Seminar develops scientific research and communication through an empirical project, with different scope.
UCR courses include substantial research projects, but the scheduled alternatives do not contain a single 15-EC artificial-intelligence bachelor project equivalent.
The genuine 30-EC minor remains open choice space rather than being assigned an invented subject.

notes.text: Groningen provides a dedicated artificial-intelligence degree with compulsory programming, formal logic, algorithms, machine learning, agent systems, language technology, cognition, specialised third-year study and a 15-EC AI project. UCR offers a strong interdisciplinary combination of computer science, data science, AI, cognitive science, psychology and philosophy, but it does not reproduce the full compulsory AI sequence or capstone structure.
